chapter: Father Al, Chinatown and Earl Hines style
title: The Chinatown neighborhood, the Black Gold and Miss Osborne
summary: He describes nearby bands and the Black Gold, and Miss Isabel Osborne's family running the place.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well back to Chinatown while you were talking about it, were there many joints in the neighborhood there?

Joints? Yeah. Well they had bands. They had bands not too far from that. It was, Black Gold used to be on, you know where that hotel is, Foster's Hotel? Yeah. Well that's where the Black Gold was. What's that, Seventh and La Salle? Yeah. Well, Miss Isabelle Osborne, her brother, Nick Patterson, he was a former officer in the whole eastern force, he used to have that place. And I used to work for his sister, you know, Miss Patterson, Miss Osborne. And her husband was named Alfred, and he had a son named Alfred, there were so many. The world was full of owls. Yeah. And he started calling me Father Owls, you understand? Well I mean, of course I had interpretations of irons and different things like, you want me to play a piece of that way?
